description: Whether tapping a search row toggles a selection instead of adding the food immediately. True when the query was split into more than one ingredient phrase — the X-Segment-Count header, NEVER a client-side space count, because the server segments with greedy longest-match probes against the index and "pomme de terre" is one term. Recipes are the exception and always add immediately: a recipe is not one of the query's terms, it unpacks into a whole meal on its own. A missing or unparseable header must be read as 1, which degrades to single-add rather than to a broken picker.

cases.why: The common case, and the one that must cost nothing: one term typed, one tap, food added. If this ever returned true the feature would have made ordinary search worse.
Three terms means the person is composing a meal, so a tap accumulates a selection they confirm once instead of forcing three search-type-tap cycles.

THE EXCEPTION, and the reason this suite exists. A recipe unpacks into several rows by itself, so it is not one of the query's terms and checkbox semantics do not apply. A port that drops this branch makes recipes un-addable on any two-word query, silently.
An Open Food Facts product is an ordinary selectable row — the recipe exception is about recipes specifically, not about "anything that is not a curated ingredient".
productType is optional on the wire. An absent value must not accidentally take the recipe branch — the exception is for rows that ARE recipes, and an unknown row is not one.
The server returns segment count 0 for a blank query, and a client that read `> 1` as `!== 1` would toggle here. Reachable while the field is being cleared.
